transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you and what brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've been losing a lot of weight recently. Lately, I've only been eating very small amounts of food.
How do you feel about your current body weight and shape, and do you feel an intense fear of gaining weight?

I have an overwhelming, terrifying fear of gaining even a single pound; it makes me feel completely out of control. When I look in the mirror, I still see so much fat and feel like I need to lose more to have any self-worth. Keeping my weight as low as possible is the only way I can feel okay about myself.

latest_inference.note: The patient's clinical presentation—severe restriction of food intake leading to weight loss, an intense, irrational fear of gaining weight, and a distorted body image where they perceive themselves as overweight despite objective weight loss—strongly aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Anorexia Nervosa. Bulimia Nervosa and Binge-Eating Disorder have been excluded due to the absence of binge-eating or compensatory behaviors mentioned, and Major Depressive Disorder is less likely to be the primary diagnosis given the specific focus on body image and weight control.
